## Natural history notes

A medium-sized tiger moth characterized by dark forewings crossed with pale cream to yellowish “harness-like” lines, along with brighter hindwings that may show orange, pinkish, or yellow tones with dark markings. In Florida, the Harnessed Tiger Moth is found in fields, roadsides, pine flatwoods, forest edges, gardens, and other open or semi-open habitats with low vegetation. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the fuzzy caterpillars feed on a variety of low herbaceous plants and help transfer plant growth into the broader food web for birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
